topic: Conditional investment decision to extend operations to 2036
wiki_text: In 2025, Dutch partners Gasunie and Vopak (operating through EemsEnergyTerminal) took a conditional investment decision to extend operations of their FSRU-based LNG import terminal at Eemshaven beyond 2027, with the intention of keeping the terminal operational until 2036. The terminal, which began operations on 8 September 2022, uses two chartered floating units — the ~170,000 m3 FSRU Energos Igloo (owned by Energos Infrastructure) and the ~26,000 m3 barge-based FSRU Eemshaven LNG (owned by Exmar) — and has a nameplate capacity of about 8 bcm/year, with stated ambition to reach 9-10 bcm/year through technical optimization/debottlenecking. The extension is conditional (subject to final commitments) and does not change the current nameplate capacity.

VTTI and Hoegh Evi are developing the Zeeland Energy Terminal (ZET), a proposed FSRU-based LNG import terminal to be sited at either Sloehaven (Vlissingen) or Braakmanhaven (Terneuzen) and connected directly to the Dutch national gas grid. The formal permitting process — designated a project of strategic interest by the Dutch government — was launched on 2 May 2025 with publication of the Notification of Intent. The first phase of the permit procedure was completed on 26 August 2025 with the response bundle, and on 12 December 2025 the partners published the draft Scope and Level of Detail Memorandum (draft NRD) and participation proposal, with public feedback collected from 12 December 2025 to 22 January 2026 and an information meeting held 7 January 2026 in Nieuwdorp. As of the latest reporting the project remained pre-FID, with projected start-up in 2028/2029 pending permits, a final investment decision and market commitments.
